title: Canonical Boolean pop machine
statement: For $k$ work tapes and a selected tape $i<k$, define a machine with states $\{\mathrm{halt},0,1\}$ whose initial state is halt. In the halt state it stays on the input tape, writes blank on tape $i$, and outputs the bit currently scanned on tape $i$, treating a blank as $0$; in state $b\in\{0,1\}$ it stays on the input tape and outputs $b$.
hypotheses_covered: The selected work tape $i$ is one of the $k$ tapes
caveat: The helper definitions for the two action constructors are omitted, so the precise movement, write, output, and successor-state behavior cannot be fully confirmed from this snippet alone.
